topic: AI CERTs AI+ Robotics Practitioner (AT-420) certification exam preparation - a vendor-neutral credential at the intersection of artificial intelligence and robotics, covering robotics and AI foundations, autonomous systems and intelligent agents, robotics development frameworks (ROS and simulation), deep learning and reinforcement learning for robots, generative AI and NLP for human-robot interaction, robotic process automation, and AI ethics, safety, and future trends in robotics
exam_format: Online, proctored exam with flexible scheduling: 50 multiple-choice and multiple-response questions, 90 minutes, passing score 70% (35/50). The bundle includes one free retake and a digital badge. IMPORTANT: AI CERTs delivers this as a TRAINING-PLUS-EXAM package (instructor-led or self-paced course + official exam) - there is no advertised standalone exam-only path, so this course is positioned as independent companion/concept prep, not a replacement for the official AI CERTs training. The ~$249 figure is an approximate exam-voucher estimate; bundle pricing via Authorized Training Partners is higher - confirm current pricing on the AI CERTs site.
question_types: multiple choice (single answer, exactly 4 options) and multiple select clearly marked as 'Select TWO/THREE'
audience: Robotics engineers, mechanical engineers, AI/ML specialists, IT specialists and system integrators, and students or recent graduates who want to prove applied knowledge at the AI-plus-robotics intersection. Only basic familiarity with AI concepts is required to start; some Python helps for the applied sections. Fits the catalog's AI cluster and opens a brand-new robotics/physical-AI vertical - cross-sell the NVIDIA NCA-AMAD (physical AI) and agentic-AI courses.
author: Aseem Mankotia

domains.name: Robotics and AI Foundations
domains.notes: Consolidates AT-420 modules 1-2: introduction to robotics and artificial intelligence, and understanding AI and robotics mechanics (sensors, actuators, perception-plan-act loop, kinematics at a conceptual level, how AI changes classical robotics). Core vocabulary the rest of the exam builds on.

domains.name: Autonomous Systems and Intelligent Agents
domains.notes: AT-420 module 3: autonomy levels, intelligent agents, perception and decision-making, SLAM/navigation concepts, and how agentic AI maps onto autonomous robots.

domains.name: AI and Robotics Development Frameworks
domains.notes: AT-420 module 4: robotics development frameworks and tooling - ROS/ROS 2 concepts, simulation environments (Gazebo, Isaac Sim at a conceptual level), middleware, and the robotics software stack. Highest-value practical chapter.

domains.name: Deep Learning for Robotics
domains.notes: AT-420 module 5: deep learning algorithms applied to robotics - computer vision for perception, object detection, sensor fusion, and neural control. Conceptual, with robotics-specific examples.

domains.name: Reinforcement Learning for Robotics
domains.notes: AT-420 module 6: reinforcement learning in robotics - reward design, sim-to-real transfer, policy learning for locomotion and manipulation, and where RL fits vs classical control.

domains.name: Generative AI and NLP for Human-Robot Interaction
domains.notes: Consolidates AT-420 modules 7-8: generative AI for robotic creativity, and natural language processing for human-robot interaction (voice commands, LLM-driven robot instruction, conversational interfaces). One of the heaviest combined areas - give it strong coverage.

domains.name: Applied Robotics: Use-Cases and RPA
domains.notes: Consolidates AT-420 modules 9 and 11: practical activities and real-world use-cases, plus exploring AI with Robotic Process Automation (RPA) - industrial, warehouse, healthcare, and service robotics, and software RPA as the 'digital robot' counterpart. Scenario-heavy.

domains.name: Emerging Technologies and Future Trends
domains.notes: Consolidates AT-420 modules 10 and 13: emerging technologies and innovation in robotics, and innovations/future trends in AI and robotics - humanoids, physical AI, foundation models for robotics (e.g., VLA models), swarm robotics, and where the field is heading.

domains.name: AI Ethics, Safety, and Policy in Robotics
domains.notes: AT-420 module 12: AI ethics, safety, and policy as applied to robots - physical safety, human oversight, liability, bias, and responsible deployment of autonomous physical systems.

extra_guidance: AI+ Robotics Practitioner (AT-420) from AI CERTs is a VENDOR-NEUTRAL AI+robotics credential and opens a brand-new robotics/physical-AI vertical for this catalog (no robotics course exists yet). Exam facts: 50 multiple-choice/multiple-response questions, 90 minutes, 70% to pass (35/50), online proctored, one free retake, digital badge. The exam blueprint has THIRTEEN official domains - the nine domains above CONSOLIDATE them for a clean 12-chapter course; cover all thirteen module topics. The full official module list is: (1) Introduction to Robotics and AI, (2) Understanding AI and Robotics Mechanics, (3) Autonomous Systems and Intelligent Agents, (4) AI and Robotics Development Frameworks, (5) Deep Learning Algorithms in Robotics, (6) Reinforcement Learning in Robotics, (7) Generative AI for Robotic Creativity, (8) NLP for Human-Robot Interaction, (9) Practical Activities and Use-Cases, (10) Emerging Technologies and Innovation in Robotics, (11) Exploring AI with Robotic Process Automation (RPA), (12) AI Ethics, Safety, and Policy, (13) Innovations and Future Trends in AI and Robotics. ACCURACY: present module/topic NAMES as official and the per-domain PERCENTAGES as approximate (AI CERTs publishes small per-module weights that the consolidation above sums; say 'approximate' in chapter 1). POSITIONING/HONESTY (important): AI CERTs sells this as a training+exam bundle with no advertised exam-only path, so position the course plainly as independent companion/concept prep that builds the knowledge to pass - NOT as a replacement for the official AI CERTs training. State this in chapter 1 and the description. Ground content vendor-neutrally: ROS/ROS 2, Gazebo and Isaac Sim (conceptual), classical control vs learning-based control, CV/sensor fusion, RL and sim-to-real, LLM/VLA-driven robots, and robot safety standards at a conceptual level. Labs are tabletop/architecture exercises (design a ROS node graph, plan a sim-to-real RL pipeline, spec an LLM voice-control stack for a robot arm, build a robot-safety risk register) - no physical hardware required. Final chapter = full 90-minute / 50-question / 70%-pass exam simulation with time-management strategy. Keep all practice questions scenario-based with plausible distractors; scan the bank per the pipeline compliance rules (no 'guaranteed pass'/'first attempt' language). Marketing angle: 'Break into AI + Robotics - complete, vendor-neutral prep for the AI+ Robotics Practitioner credential covering ROS, deep/reinforcement learning, generative AI for robots, and physical AI.'
